scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Walk through an airport gate with keys in your pocket, and it beeps. How can it sense metal it can't see?

scenes.name: coil
scenes.text: A metal detector has a coil of wire. Pulses of current through it create a changing magnetic field.

scenes.name: eddy
scenes.text: When that field passes through metal, it makes small swirling currents inside the metal, called eddy currents.

scenes.name: echo
scenes.text: Those currents create their own tiny magnetic field, like an echo coming back.

scenes.name: receive
scenes.text: A receiver coil, or the same coil between pulses, picks up that echo and the electronics sound the alarm.

scenes.name: types
scenes.text: Different metals respond differently, so some detectors can guess if it's iron, coins or gold.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: Plastic, paper and skin don't respond, which is why airports also use X-ray scanners for bags.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Pulse a field, make currents, catch the echo. Follow for more on how things really work.
